title: Cortex
tagline: A reliability kernel for AI agents
description: Coding agents are capable, but you can't trust their output without reviewing it — and reviewing costs as much as the work. I inverted the usual bet: instead of a smarter agent, build the machinery around it. A deny-by-default reference monitor, unforgeable content-bound receipts, trust-graded sandboxes, and deterministic oracle gates let interchangeable models do real work on a codebase you never have to read to trust. It composes decades-proven OS-security patterns — reference monitors, privilege separation, capability tokens — into a trust kernel for agent software production, built contract-first and self-hosting: every module ships through the same gates it will one day enforce.

links.title: ONI vs My Agent Ready Architecture
links.description: Software architecture has not caught up with agent-first coding yet. I built an npm package so repos keep agent speed without losing planning time, audit trails, or architecture shape — modular boundaries, contracts, versioned dev logs, agent-readable JSON audits, prompt versioning, evals, and patch/rollback context stronger than git alone. Inspired by Oxygen Not Included systems thinking; tested with multi-agent pipelines up to 500 agents and designed to grow naturally toward microservices.
